title: legal-redlines-scratchpad-maya-patel
content:
Quick personal scratchpad for recent customer contract redline (ACME Corp).

Goal: capture clauses to watch, quick negotiation talking points, and open questions for Legal ops before I submit final redline. Mostly shorthand - will clean up before adding to PR.

1) Limitation of Liability / Cap
- Customer proposes unlimited liability for data breach (red flag).
- Our baseline: cap = greater of $X or 12 months fees (we usually push for 12 months fees; internal policy says do not accept uncapped direct damages).
- Talking point: propose mutual cap tied to fees; carve out gross negligence/fraud.
- Ask Legal: can we accept carve-out for IP indemnity claims? prefer cap applies to all but IP indemnity.

2) Indemnity / IP infringement
- Customer wants us to indemnify for infringement arising from their prompts/data (too broad).
- We should limit to claims arising from our models/software as delivered, not customer content or prompts.
- Add: customer indemnifies for claims arising from their content, prompts, or misuse of the service.

3) Data usage & model training
- Customer asks for explicit prohibition on using their data to improve models - common ask.
- Options: (a) explicit no-training clause (customer PII concerns), (b) allow aggregated/anonymous telemetry only.
- If we agree to no-training, ensure we can still use operational telemetry for debugging/ops (anonymized).
- Negotiation point: offer a data-privacy addendum or a paid private-deploy option (Dedicated/Private) if they need stronger guarantees.

4) Security / SOC / Audit rights
- Customer requests on-site audits and unlimited access to logs (problem).
- Counter: provide SOC 2 report and right to audit via third-party, with reasonable notice and scope; no unfettered access to infra.
- Add: define frequency, notice period, and redaction rules for logs (remove other customers).

5) SLA / Availability / Remedies
- Customer wants 99.99% guaranteed with financial credits; check what Dedicated vs Hosted supports.
- For hosted API: offer SLA consistent with product page; for Dedicated, higher SLA possible but tie to reserved capacity and breach thresholds.
- Remedies: credits capped (e.g., credits up to monthly invoice); avoid termination right for single outage unless repeated.

6) Termination / Data return/destruction
- On termination customer wants immediate deletion + certified deletion of backups. We can commit to deletion from active systems within X days, and reasonable efforts for backups (point-in-time retention policies).
- Add: timeline for data export (e.g., 30 days) and certified deletion process.

7) Confidentiality definition
- Customer defines Confidential Info too broadly (e.g., includes residuals and non-identifiable outputs).
- Push for carve-out: residuals/aggregated metrics not confidential; allow model improvements from general learnings except customer-specific PII.

8) Export controls / sanctions
- Ensure clause allows us to comply with applicable export laws; add right to suspend service if use violates sanctions.

9) Subprocessors / third-party infra
- Customer wants approval for subprocessors. Offer notice + objection right within narrow timeline; cannot unreasonably withhold for standard cloud infra.

10) Warranty / Disclaimers
- They want broad uptime/quality warranties. Maintain standard warranty: service as described, no promise of specific outputs/accuracy. Include ML-specific disclaimer: outputs may be incorrect and should be validated.

11) Change of law / regulatory compliance (esp. EU)
- If customer is EU regulated, check requirements on data residency. Suggest Private deployment or dedicated region.

12) Escrow / source code
- Customer asked for code escrow in long negotiation - expensive for us. For large enterprise deals, consider alternative: extended support + higher SLA, but avoid source code escrow unless legal recommends.

Open questions / TODOs
- Q1: Confirm cap baseline number - what is acceptable for mid-market vs enterprise? (ask Sales for expected ARR).
- Q2: Is there an approved language for "no model training" clause that still allows anonymized telemetry? (ask Privacy team).
- Q3: Check if we can accept on-site data center visits for Dedicated (SRE ops input).

Negotiation snippets to try in calls:
- "We can mirror most of the customer's protections if we keep liability cap mutual and tied to fees - helps balance risk for both sides."
- "If data residency is a hard requirement, we can propose Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) as a paid option - that'll meet the compliance ask."
- "We agree to provide SOC 2 and periodic third-party audit reports; on-site audits are possible via a defined process and scope with reasonable notice."

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep redline comments short; add cross-link to SOC 2 docs and privacy addendum.
- Bring Sales into talks early if they signal >$250k ARR - different negotiation playbook.
- Remember: don't concede to uncapped liability or broad training prohibition for hosted API customers unless compensated.

---
